items.article: Thousands of flights could be impacted through higher fares or cancelled routes if an airport on a remote Pacific Ocean island doesn't get a $100 million dollar fix. The Midway Atoll airport has no commercial service, but is vital for airlines. Thousands of flights could be impacted through higher fares or cancelled routes if an airport on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean doesn't get a $100 million dollar fix. The airport on Midway Atoll, 1,300 miles northwest of Honolulu, has no commercial air service but is an emergency landing option for thousands of flights crossing the Pacific each year. If airlines lose the option to land there when they have an engine failure, they would need to use longer, more expensive routes or cut destinations entirely. The FAA is weighing whether or not it should fund these major repairs at Henderson Field (MDY) on Midway Atoll. According to the agency, the airport's infrastructure is "deteriorating" and the facilities will need significant fixes within the next few years. The airport currently receives $2.5 million per year from the FAA and $2.6 million from the Fish and Wildlife Service -- but the estimated cost for the repairs the airport needs, which include "milling, repaving, and seawall repairs," exceeds $100 million. items.key: ai:how ukraine is taking down putin's deadly new drones
items.text: How Ukraine is taking down Putin’s deadly new drones
items.article: The air defence battle for supremacy over both Russian and Ukrainian cities is becoming a more critical part of the conflict Russia’s latest jet-powered attack drones are forcing Ukraine into a lethal arms race against the clock. A new generation of Russian Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones – which are quicker, more sophisticated and harder for Kyiv’s air defences to intercept – have been hammering its cities. Kyiv is now scrambling to develop defences that can catch them before they reach their targets, with Ukrainian companies developing a new generation of high-speed interceptors designed specifically to hunt them down. It is a game of cat and mouse with deadly consequences . Ukrainian drone maker Wild Hornets says its new Sting S interceptor has destroyed several Geran-5 drones during combat testing, along with roughly a dozen of the slower Geran-4s. It said the interceptions took place over recent weeks and that it plans to begin mass production once all of its testing is complete. The Sting S is one of several interceptor systems that Ukrainian forces are combat-testing in real time in the skies over Ukraine, including the WIV SPYS , developed alongside Germany, and the Zorelit v5 and Zirka, designed to automatically detect and destroy incoming attack drones. The race to develop interceptor systems is a striking new reality of the war: Every time Russia updates its attack drones, Ukraine has to ramp up the weapons used to destroy them, sometimes in a matter of months.

items.article: Connor is motivated by a desire to give his son Alfie 'a childhood he didn't have' An ex-soldier who began his small side hustle 'for some extra cash' in lockdown now earns up to £40,000 a month and has quit his full-time job. He said his new business has allowed him to give his son "a childhood (he) didn’t have", which he says is "worth more than anything". Connor Stone, 31, joined the British Army in 2019 and began reselling hard-to-find items, including hair clippers, weights and outdoor heaters, during the Covid-19 pandemic. He gradually began selling clothes from his "own wardrobe" too, making a "few hundred" pounds a month, before leaving the Army in 2024 for a "fresh start" after he and his wife Lauren, 32, suffered seven miscarriages while struggling to conceive. Connor took a job in logistics at DHL while continuing to resell, eventually joining Whatnot - a live- shopping marketplace - and began to sell items in seconds. Within six months, he said he was making in a week what he earned in a month at DHL, prompting him to quit his job and pursue reselling full-time. He now sells around 300 items a day, hosts five livestreams a week and works with suppliers across the globe, while he and Lauren welcomed their son Alfie (now 11 months) in October 2025. Connor is now looking forward to taking Alfie to Disneyland for his first birthday with his earnings, and hopes to grow the business even further. items.key: ai:budget 2027 update: from income tax to energy excises and childcare – here's what we know so far
items.text: Budget 2027 update: From income tax to energy excises and childcare – here’s what we know so far
items.article: Spending of €7 billion planned with €1.5 billion in tax reductions Budget 2027 , to be presented on October 6th, is due to involve a package of €8.5 billion, with €7 billion in additional spending and €1.5 billion in tax reductions. The cost-of-living issue will be a key focus across the whole package. While the €7 billion figure is large, an increase of about 6 per cent on this year, much of this money is already effectively allocated to various budgets to keep pace with inflation. There will, however, be key decisions to be made in areas such as health – which is already running well above budget for this year – and education. And, of course, in welfare, one of the mainstays of any budget package, with a call to be made on levels of increase in the main rates. The €1.5 billion package leaves limited enough room for manoeuvre. [ Budget 2027: ‘Specific consideration’ for measures to tackle rising heating oil costs Opens in new window ] If the bulk of the money were directed to income tax cuts it would allow the system to be adjusted for inflation and higher wages but not much more than that.

items.text: We handed Man City the ultimate punishment and simulated 10 seasons – here's how bad things got
items.article: What would happen if Manchester City were kicked down to non-league? We asked Football Manager to find out Manchester City are set for another trophy-laden era, even if they receive the worst possible punishment after being found guilty of 114 Premier League rule breaches. At least according to everyone's favourite management game, Football Manager. City, who continue to deny any wrongdoing and have appealed against the independent commission's verdict, and the rest of football are waiting to see what punishment will be meted out to the eight-time Premier League champions. Potential sanctions include expulsion from the top flight, a points deduction and a huge fine. The most severe penalty could see City booted all the way down to the National League, leading to matches against the likes of Boston United, Hornchurch and a derby with Altrincham. An awful prospect for City fans - certainly for the ones who have only known Premier League glory - but a fascinating one for everyone else. We turned to Football Manager 26's pre-game editor to simulate 10 City seasons ahead from the fifth tier. FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page After demoting City four consecutive times, we granted the highest-placed club in each division a reprieve from relegation. That handed a lifeline to West Ham United, Oxford United, Exeter City and Harrogate Town in their respective leagues.

items.text: Content creator's 'Sanatani protein breakfast' is viral. What's on his plate?
items.article: Protein-maxxing, but make it spiritual? A creator’s morning meal has caught the internet’s attention. You may have heard of a protein-rich breakfast. But have you ever heard of a “Sanatani protein breakfast”? A content creator is putting his own spin on the internet’s current obsession with protein, and his morning meal comes with a side of his spiritual belief. Tamal, who goes by the username mantra_saadhana on Instagram, says he is a vegetarian bodybuilder and a follower of Sanatana Dharma. He often shares glimpses of his diet, fitness and spiritual routine on Instagram and YouTube. Recently, he shared what he eats for breakfast, describing it as a “Sanatani protein breakfast” in the caption. Protein is one of the most essential nutrients, as we all know. Including it in your breakfast can help keep you fuller for longer, support muscle repair and maintenance, and provide sustained energy throughout the morning. For people who work out or strength train, getting enough protein throughout the day is particularly important for muscle recovery and growth. So, what does Tamal's "Sanatani protein breakfast” look like? His plate includes tofu, yoghurt, tomatoes, cucumber, an apple and bread. In the video, he describes the meal as being “high in protein”. Tamal cuts tofu into small cubes and cooks it in ghee with jeera (cumin), hing(asafoetida), and haldi (turmeric), before adding salt and black pepper. He then mashes the tofu slightly and lets it cook for a few more minutes.
